Something I can do for you?
{NICKNAME}, Paimon...
Oh? You're acquainted, then?
Yes. They visited Hiisi Island yesterday — we had dinner together.
Allow me to introduce you. {NICKNAME}, Paimon... This is Nefer, boss of the Curatorium of Secrets.
Pleasure to meet you.
They are travelers who arrived in Nod-Krai just yesterday. Greeted by the birds and beasts of this land, they are kind-hearted souls who walk in the moonlight's glow...
(Hmm? Ha, interesting...)

dialogue.sit: Actually, I, uh...

dialogue.t: Thank you, Lauma, but you need not have introduced them. They are great heroes, renowned throughout the nations beyond our borders.
Oh, really...?
Do not forget, I deal in information. Just because most people in Nod-Krai pay scant attention to foreign affairs, that does not mean the same goes for the Curatorium of Secrets.
They're the heroes everyone was talking about before — the ones who saved Natlan during the Abyss crisis.

dialogue.sit: (Help... I've never felt this uncomfortable being praised before... How am I supposed to explain what happened last night now?)

dialogue.t: I see... We Frostmoon Scions seldom leave our domain, so I had not heard of your heroic deeds. Please, forgive my ignorance.
Hehe, it's no big deal, we were hoping to keep a low profile anyway. If we had to list all of our titles and good deeds, we'd be talking till sundown, and then some!

dialogue.sit: Paimon...!

dialogue.t: Huh? What's wrong? Still not feeling great?
So, what brings you both to the Curatorium today?
Ohhh, so basically, we were just eating when we overheard people talking about how the Frostmoon Scions' relic had been stolen... and then he(she) dragged Paimon over here.
(Mm... I see.)
Ah, I see! So you came over here because you were worried about Lauma? A combination truly befitting of great heroes — strong at arms and pure of heart.

dialogue.sit: (I can't take this much longer...)

dialogue.t: In that case, Lauma, I've got a suggestion.
Why not ask these battle-hardened heroes to take the commission for you? Honestly, it's a little beyond the means of such a modest establishment as ours.
Your "modest establishment," unable to handle a commission? You just don't want to take it, do you?
You're right — I do not.
What kind of commission is this?
Surely it's not... to recover your stolen relic?
Yes, that is it.
Recovering the relic is both my duty as a Moonchanter and a step toward fulfilling the promise I made {NICKNAME} — to help uncover the truth of the past.
But Nefer has already declined our commission multiple times.
And yet, just as it always has, the moon will continue to illuminate the sky above the Curatorium.
Come night or day, may the Moon Goddess keep you.
...Enough of that.

dialogue.sit: I'm sorry, everyone...
There's something I need to get off my chest.

dialogue.t: (So... according to him(her), he(she) never came into contact with the relic... so he(she) suspects his sister(her brother) may have taken it.)
Mm... I understand.

dialogue.sit: I'm truly sorry...

dialogue.t: ...The Frostmoon Scions' secret chamber has remained hidden from the world for generations. But the reason outsiders are forbidden entry is not only to prevent theft.
Within the chamber lie ancient trials, challenges designed to test the worthiness of those who enter. To intrude without rightful cause is a most perilous act indeed.
So please, don't be too hard on yourself, {NICKNAME}. The fact that you made it through those trials proves your right to stand before the relic.
To put it simply... the Moon Marrow itself has deemed you worthy.

dialogue.sit: ...You're not angry with me?

dialogue.t: No. Your honesty tells me everything — you never sought to take the Moon Marrow for yourself.

As for what happened at the end... I suspect the chamber's protection mechanism may have been activated. Among those who entered the final chamber, there was either someone with impure intent, or else... an Abyssal presence.
The Abyss?

dialogue.sit: My sister(brother)...
...Can indeed wield the power of the Abyss.

dialogue.t: Perhaps that's why, then. Either way, the Moon Marrow was taken...
...And I believe you, so the problem remains the same. I need to recover our relic.

dialogue.sit: I'll help you.
I want to find my sister(brother) too...

dialogue.t: See? Didn't I tell you it would all work out in the end?
But before everyone starts celebrating, forgive me for asking just one more thing... Are you absolutely sure your sister(brother) took the relic?
What do you mean? Weren't they the only ones inside at the time?
Who knows? Think about it — after your sister(brother) broke the seal with Abyssal power, what was to stop someone else from following you in there?
Hmm... In theory, nothing.
And as it just so happens, I received a tip-off from one of my sources earlier this morning...
Word is, today of all days, the Fatui suddenly called off their search for the relic.
...What?
Huh? Why?
Well, either they woke up this morning and suddenly decided they'd lost all interest, or...

dialogue.sit: They already have it.

dialogue.t: Exactly.

dialogue.sit: (But... no... Lumine(Aether) couldn't possibly be working with the Fatui...)

dialogue.t: Are you wondering if your sister(brother) might be in cahoots with the Fatui?
Which is why I asked: Are you absolutely sure your sister(brother) took the relic?
Or to put it another way... Do you really know your sister(brother)?

dialogue.sit: (She's right... The truth is, I really don't know what Lumine(Aether) is trying to do here...)

dialogue.t: In other words... it's highly likely that the Fatui already have the Moon Marrow.
So basically, all we need to do is find our way into that Fatui research facility, and we should be able to get to the bottom of this, right?
Congratulations, you've found your answer! Looks like the Curatorium won't need to lift a finger this time.
Well, Lauma, there we are... On behalf of our longstanding cooperation, and the great hero by your side, I'll waive your consultation fee — but just this once.
...You're really not planning on helping us?
I think I've helped more than enough already.
If we're to stand any chance of infiltrating that facility, we'll need the help of a specialist.
*sigh* Just so you don't get the wrong idea, let me make myself crystal clear...
The Curatorium of Secrets has always striven to abide by a policy of strict neutrality. We do not take sides with any faction in Nod-Krai.
I cannot help the leader of the Frostmoon Scions sneak into a Fatui facility. That would make me their enemy.
When one of their Harbingers asked me to help them infiltrate your territory, I gave them the same answer — "No."
Alright, I understand.
But I do have one final request... I promise it's my last.
...It had better be.
No matter who it is, I want you to help us persuade the next person who walks through that door to join us.
(What is she up to...?)
You're that desperate for help? What if it's a member of the Fatui?
It doesn't matter. You're welcome to tell them everything, even about our plans to infiltrate the Experimental Design Bureau.
All I'm asking is for you to say one thing, just one thing to help persuade them. If you do that, I promise I won't ask you for anything else.
Made up your mind?
Fine, fine. I'll play along with your little game.
Besides, as long as I'm not personally involved, no one can accuse us of taking sides...
Boss, I'm back!
You won't believe the luck I've been having today! Remember you sent me to find that runaway cat, yeah? And you said I'd only be back after dark?
Well, guess what? Right after I left the house, this big ibis flew over, and the missing cat was right in its claws! And once it got close, it loosened its grip, and—
...Ahh! Boss, you're... meeting clients? I'm so sorry, I'll... get out of your way!

dialogue.sit: (That ibis... must've been sent by Lauma...)

dialogue.t: Jahoda, dear, come here.
Huh? Me...? Uh... Is something the matter? Oh, uh... Hi there...
My dear Jahoda, I have a... request.
(Yikes! Why does the boss sound so... scary? Did I do something wrong?)
Would you be so kind as to accompany these three delightful clients of ours and help them infiltrate the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau?
(What is going on here!? Boss usually just says things like "Hey, go do this," or "You, go take care of that." Why is she being so... scarily polite?)
(And... Wait a sec, the Fatui's research facility!? That's basically a death sentence!)
Made your mind up yet, my dear?
Uhhh... I... I...
(What is up with Boss today? Am I supposed to say yes to this!? Or... or maybe it's because the mission's too risky, so she's actually looking out for me...?)
(Why is everyone looking at me like that!? Is this... some kind of test? I—I can't let Boss down... Can I?)
Have you... made up... your mind?
Ahhh! I... Uh, umm... Th—That's... Sure, why not?
Really? You really don't mind helping us?
Huh? Oh, umm... Yes... I—I mean, no! Of course I... I mean, I... I guess I do...?
Thanks so much! We owe ya big time!
On behalf of the Frostmoon Scions, too — thank you, Jahoda, for your help.
(What the...!? Seriously, what just happened?)
(Why does the boss look so fed up? Oh no, was I supposed to turn them down...?)
(Ha... All that mentoring, time spent teaching her how to deal with different factions... in one ear and out the other...)
Nefer...
You got what you wanted. You promised that was it.
I know this goes against your principles. I won't forget the favor.
Ha... Trying to get me to change my mind now?
Of course not. I just wanted to say thank you.
So... Thank you.
Jahoda, we'll leave the planning to you. Let's discuss the details elsewhere.
Huh? O—Okay...
(What have I got myself into...?)
Oh — by the way, Jahoda, before you go...
Uh... What is it, boss?
...You're fired.
...Huh?
Effective immediately. As in, this exact moment.
The Curatorium will take you back, of course — but only once you've completed this commission for our three clients.
...What!?
Is there some issue? Well, here's the upside — without me taking a cut from your commission, you'll earn more.
...Seriously, can someone explain what is going on here!?

dialogue.sit: After Jahoda is finally brought up to speed, you all agree on a plan to infiltrate the Fatui research facility the following night...

dialogue.t: Are we sure Jahoda's alright? She looked totally crushed just now...
She'll be fine, she's just in shock. But one thing's for sure — the Curatorium's professional standards are beyond question.
The fact that she only requested one day to prepare says it all.
As an apology, I'll ask my animal friends to help her out more often in the future...
Also... Thank you for being honest with me, {NICKNAME}. It means a lot.

dialogue.sit: It was my fault in the first place...

dialogue.t: Was it really, though?
As far as I see it, trusting your family is never "wrong." In this case, let's call it... a misjudgment.
But the truth is, we all make mistakes every now and then. What matters is how we deal with the consequences.
So... In return for your sincerity, there's something I'd like to share with the two of you as well.
Oh? What is it?
...Perhaps it is something best said under the moon's gentle light. Would the two of you meet me on Hiisi Island tonight?

dialogue.sit: No problem.

dialogue.t: Hmm, it does sound important... You're right, there's too many people here. Somewhere quieter makes a lot more sense.
Thank you both for understanding. Then let us meet beneath the moonlight.
Lauma, we're here!
Huh? Lauma, are you... praying?
I am indeed... For the moment I was born, my people exclaimed: "Behold: eyes like the moonlit tide, antlers like the crescent moon, and blood that glimmers silver as the moon's reflection..."
From as far back as I can remember, I was revered as the "Frostmoon's Emissary" and the "Moon-Tide Maiden"...
The first words I ever learned were prayers to the Frostmoon... the first gestures, those of our sacred rites.
Wow, that... must have been tough.
Back then, I didn't know any better. It all just seemed so... natural.
The Frostmoon Scions' bloodline has long since begun to run thin. Nowadays, even those of us with antlers are few and far between, let alone those attuned to the power of kuuvahki.
But I...
Whoa... Your antlers are so pretty...

They say it's an extraordinarily rare condition... once in a century, if that. I am unusually sensitive to the moonlight, as well as to the kuuvahki's ebb and flow. As a child, I could barely sleep because of it.
Oh no... It was that serious?
To others, fluctuations in kuuvahki are something you easily get used to — like a gentle tide lapping away at the shore.
But to me, that same tide is a towering tsunami, a surging swell crashing against me...
Of course, as the years went by, I learned how to suppress my senses — and my power — enough to keep it all from overwhelming me.
But because of that... I also had to walk the path of concealment.
Concealment...?
From the moment I was first taught to pray, my kin would point up to the night sky, telling me: "That, Lauma, is the Frostmoon — the last of the moons, the sole surviving truth."
But I would ask them in response: "Why? Why can't I feel anything from it at all?"
Later, I came to understand that they simply could not tell where the real tide was coming from. They couldn't sense it... the true moon beyond the sky's veil.

dialogue.sit: (Is Lauma talking about the false sky? So the true Frost Moon... lies beyond it?)

dialogue.t: "The moon is false"... I reached that conclusion long ago.
But there was no one I could tell, not a single soul... At least, not until now.
"Am I the one who's wrong? Is it the moon that is false, or my own senses?" ...I asked myself such questions, time and time again.

dialogue.sit: Your intuitions were correct.
The sky above Teyvat... is a lie.

dialogue.t: Thank you... {NICKNAME}.
When you called yourself a Descender, I had a feeling you might be able to confirm what I had always suspected.
And now that you have, it's exactly as I imagined. I feel... relieved.
Ohhh, Paimon kinda gets why you couldn't tell anyone now... It's not easy to change people's minds on something they've believed for hundreds of years.
That's what I meant by "concealment"...
I knew too much, so I had no choice but to keep my people in the dark... Every prayer I offer feels like a lie to keep myself going.

dialogue.sit: (So that's what she meant when she asked me that question...)
("If you were aware of something, a secret that could hurt your family... Would you be honest with them, or try to hide it?")

dialogue.t: {NICKNAME}... You've already met our "Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar", haven't you?

dialogue.sit: ...Yes.

dialogue.t: Huh? When was that, and more importantly, when were you planning on telling Paimon!?

dialogue.sit: That night when I went out walking alone...

dialogue.t: Ah, no wonder...
What did you think of her?

dialogue.sit: A little... up in the clouds?
And a bit lonely, too.

dialogue.t: What exactly do you mean by "up in the clouds"...
I understand what you mean. She is quite indifferent to the world outside herself. But... I find it hard to hold that against her.

dialogue.sit: Does that mean...
...You've met her too?

dialogue.t: Yes. It was shortly after the fall of the Ancient Moon's Remnants.
I asked her what the Frostmoon Scions meant to her, and why she left in the first place.
Yeah, so, why did she...?
Perhaps... it's better if you ask her yourselves. Things tend to get lost in translation when you speak on someone's behalf.
What I can say for certain is this. Even when I had no one to confide in, I still had a family... I still had the Frostmoon Scions.
But that girl, born beneath the moonlight... perhaps she's never felt she had either.
The truth is, though, she might have had it all — if only the Frostmoon Scions hadn't let her down.

dialogue.sit: (Last time I saw her, she kept looking up at the sky... Was she staring at the real moon beyond the false firmament?)

dialogue.t: The Frostmoon Scions now walk a path of error. They offer their prayers to a false moon, and to a goddess who can no longer answer them.
I want to change all that.
But with the Fatui closing in on us day by day, the Frostmoon Scions must stand united — now more than ever. I just... need to wait for the right moment.
Lady Lauma, Lady Lauma!
Kapy...? Has Kaarina's condition deteriorated again?
{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we'll have to continue this conversation later.
Wait up, we'll come too!
Why...? Did I do something wrong? I've been praying to the Moon Goddess every day... Why isn't she getting any better...

dialogue.sit: (The Moon Goddess is powerless to answer her prayers, just like Lauma said...)

dialogue.t: Kapy, I need you to wait outside. I'm about to start her treatment.
Is there anything we can do to help...?
Just... don't be alarmed by what you're about to see. And please, don't let her mother see it...

dialogue.sit: (Is that... a knife!?)
(Silver blood, and... medicine powder?)

dialogue.t: Shh... Please... Help me keep this a secret...
She looks much better now... But Lauma, was that...?
...A medicine prescribed by a local doctor. For ordinary people, my blood has the power to counteract any adverse reactions to kuuvahki.

dialogue.sit: (Lauma's hands are covered in scars... Has she been secretly treating people like this all along...?)

dialogue.t: *sigh* So now you know another of my little secrets...
I had hoped to guide the Scions out of error before Kaarina's illness reached this stage. But clearly... I was too late.

dialogue.sit: (Changing old beliefs is never easy... Some are simply too deeply ingrained, just like this girl's mother's...)
This isn't your fault.
It isn't anybody's fault.

dialogue.t: My life... is as hidden from sight as the far side of the moon. Yet people only look to the bright side for guidance.
If the day ever came when the two sides were reversed... could they truly accept it?

dialogue.sit: (Why am I thinking of Lumine(Aether) right now...? Has she(he) been forced to keep a part of her(his) life hidden too?)
(If it was Lumine(Aether)...)
If it was family...
...They'd understand.

dialogue.t: Hearing you say that... puts my heart at ease.
Mm-hmm! And if there's anything we can do to help the Frostmoon Scions, just let us know!
Our priority right now is reclaiming our relic from the Fatui.
But I now understand... that the day I will tell everyone the truth is no longer far off.
Wow... Paimon would never have guessed Lauma had all that bottled up inside...
Hey! Watch your step!
Aaah! Wh—What's wrong? You scared Paimon...
Whew... You scared me there, too. Almost stepped right into one of my traps...
A trap? Why would you leave a trap somewhere like this!?
Well, it's not like this is a main path... and besides, we Frostmoon Scions would recognize it instantly.

dialogue.sit: What are you trying to catch?

dialogue.t: Hmm... Alright. You don't seem like you're with the Fatui, so I guess there's no harm telling you.
Lauma asked me to set up these traps to keep the Fatui at bay.
Ohhh... Come to think of it, their three-day ultimatum is almost up now...
Yes... Hopefully, they'll back off when they realize we won't go down without a fight.
Oh, you've done a lot for the Frostmoon Scions too, just like Lauma...
...Vilemina?
Ah! It's nothing, I... I was just wondering... if any of this is really worth it.
What do you mean?
Our people... so many are stubborn, stuck in their ways... clinging to a "truth" they refuse to even question.
Do they... really deserve everything Lauma's doing for them?

dialogue.sit: They're not all like that...
...They're just afraid of change.

dialogue.t: Well, yes, but even so...
No... I—I shouldn't be saying this. Just... forget it, okay? Bye!
Huh?
(Why did I say all that... or really... why am I still doing any of this...)
(*sigh*... Either way, this will be my final night with the Frostmoon Scions...)
Well, she sure took off fast... So, are we heading back to The Flagship for a break, or what?

dialogue.sit: There's still somewhere I wanted to go...

dialogue.t: Wait, you're not thinking of visiting that "Damselette" up in cloud cuckoo land, are you...?

dialogue.sit: She must know so much...
But if she just refuses to talk again...

dialogue.t: Given who she is, pushing her won't get us anywhere. Hmm... Hey, why don't we...
...Let's bring her something tasty!
If she doesn't wanna talk, we'll have to win her over with food!

dialogue.sit: You really think it'll be that easy?

dialogue.t: Hey, no harm in trying! At the very least, it shows we're trying to be friendly.
Hmm, let's see... How about Ineffa's "9.12/10" Berries and Fried Meat, the Frostmoon Scions' boon of the day, and one of your signature dishes — your choice...
Should be a good mix of meat and veggies... there's bound to be something she likes!

dialogue.sit: (Let's give them some space so they can rest...)

dialogue.t: Alright, food's packed and ready. This is the place, right?
Why does it feel like we're going to visit a patient... Ugh, no, no, take this seriously, Paimon...
Remind me... Who are you again?

dialogue.sit: (She forgot me after a single day...?)

dialogue.t: ...A different one floats by your side today.
("A different one"!? What's that even supposed to mean? Ugh, there goes Paimon's perfect conversation starter...)
Uh, h—hi there... Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}...
Oh, there you are. Hmm. Between the two, I suppose you're cuter.
(Wait, what does she mean Paimon's less cute than that... floaty thing!?)

dialogue.sit: Columbina...

dialogue.t: ...What is it?

dialogue.sit: What's your favorite kind of food?

dialogue.t: Hmm? Is this... a treat? Or... an offering?
Uhh, let's go with "treat"! Anyway, this is all {NICKNAME}'s cooking — so please, help yourself!
(That wasn't exactly a "yes," but she didn't turn it down either. What could she be thinking?)

dialogue.sit: (Now you see what I've been dealing with...)

dialogue.t: So... What do you want to ask?
(Hey, she's actually playing along... Quick, now's our shot!)

dialogue.sit: You know the moon in the sky isn't real, don't you?

dialogue.t: I know there is only one moon in the sky. It is simply that some can see it... and some cannot.

dialogue.sit: ...What does it mean to you?

dialogue.t: The missing prologue.
What?
Huh?
(What does that mean? Isn't she going to explain herself?)

dialogue.sit: Can you tell me more about that melody? You were humming it last time, too. It must be important to you.

dialogue.t: It is all I remember from the moment of my birth — a melody, a few lines of lyrics, like a lullaby from a foggy dream.
Oh... So, who was singing it?
I do not know.
I have nothing else. Just that song.
And the Frostmoon Scions who found me... they had nothing either, but hope.
Before I even knew what was happening, they were already calling me their "Goddess." And I... had no reason to decline.
Like two lost infants unknowingly exchanged, I adopted their faith, and in return, they adopted me.
But my adoption drops you into the story halfway through. What came before was scribbled onto the wrong pages... never even bound into the book.
That sense of something missing only served to nurture their greed and doubt. And thus, I came to realize that this place was never truly my home.

dialogue.sit: Greed and doubt?

dialogue.t: "O Moon Goddess, forge weapons for us, drive out our enemies, and expand our lands..."
"O Moon Goddess, heal our wounds, ease our suffering, grant us strength..."
They asked for everything, and I obliged... until the day came when no answer could be given.
If mortals can turn to the gods when they are powerless... then who do the gods turn to when they have nothing left to give?
Uhh, you've... got Paimon there...
In those days, the Frostmoon Scions cared more for "faith" than for "truth."

dialogue.sit: (So that's why she chose to leave...)

dialogue.t: Reality rewrote the sky in words I could not understand. I did not want to read a tampered version, so I simply stopped looking.
The real beginning of my story lies up there on the moon, forever beyond my reach — like a message carved for blind hands, sealed away where no fingers can find it.
Oh, so that's how it is...
Mph...!
Wh—What's wrong!?

dialogue.sit: (The flowers... they've turned white?)

dialogue.t: *pant*... You should go...
What, now? But, you really don't look well... Did something just happen?

dialogue.sit: Is there anything we can do to help?

dialogue.t: No... Aside from answers, I have nothing else to give you in return.
This is the price... of running away from home a second time.
Running away from home...?
(Uh... Is she heading towards the food? Did all of Paimon's questions make her hungry...?)
Do you still have many questions?
I know I should offer more in return for your kindness, but I'm feeling a little worn out.
Ohhh, we're... so sorry about that!
The Tsaritsa was right. Freedom always comes with a price.
She said I could treat the Fatui as a second family, a second home... but in the end, they were no different. All they wanted in truth was my "power" as the Moon Goddess.
...I'd rather not dwell on such unhappy memories.

dialogue.sit: (Seems the Fatui can't afford to let go of such a valuable chess piece — so now they're coming for the Moon Goddess, their "Damselette in distress"...)

dialogue.t: I have fulfilled my promise to the Tsaritsa, though it has used up much of my power. So you see... this has nothing to do with betrayal.
So... you're just staying here for now, resting and recovering your strength?
Yes.
What about these flowers...?
They have grown in Nod-Krai for many generations. They're highly sensitive to the ebb and flow of kuuvahki.

dialogue.sit: (Kuuvahki...)
(So... they turn white when she's feeling weak. And when they went red that day, that was because... she was drawing upon her strength?)

dialogue.t: At times, I thought about using that relic the Frostmoon Scions had hidden away. I could sense the power within it.
But going out is such a hassle... People might see me, and I promised Lauma I wouldn't show myself to anyone. Besides, I know it's gone now anyway...
Really? Lauma asked you to stay in hiding...?
(Uh-oh, she's looking back at the food again!)
P—Paimon's still got some little krumkakes here! You could have these for dessert if you wanted...?
Lauma said she wishes to "change" the Frostmoon Scions... Which is why she asked me to stay out of sight.

I don't really understand what she meant — and to be honest, it's not something that concerns me. But I wasn't planning to see anyone, anyway. If they found their way here themselves, that's hardly my fault.

dialogue.sit: (If The Damselette appeared in front of them now, the Frostmoon Scions might very well think that their Lady Kuutar has returned to save them...)
(When you look at it that way, I guess Lauma's actions do make sense.)

dialogue.t: Lauma, the Maiden of the Grove... She is quite unlike any Frostmoon Scion I've ever met before.
After hearing my story, she actually apologized for how the Frostmoon Scions treated me back then.
She told us she feels like she's been living on the far side of the moon...
Is that so? I actually got the opposite impression...
She's been keeping her true power hidden away, afraid that people might be dazzled by its brilliance... and that they'd no longer be willing to look her way.

dialogue.sit: (Just like Kuutar back then... Maybe her light was simply too bright for anyone to see her as family?)
So, what do you wish for now?

dialogue.t: I wish to return to the moon... to the home where my story is written.
Right now... that is all I wish for.

dialogue.sit: And with that, The Damselette looks up to the sky and falls silent.
You and Paimon return to The Flagship, reflecting on everything that's happened as you prepare for tomorrow's mission...

quests.description: The secrets of this land are like an ancient song that lingers in your heart and cannot be easily dismissed… What song shall Nod-Krai play for you this night…?

quests.title: In the Shadows of Night

dialogue.t: Huh? How come you're here by yourself, Lauma? Where's Jahoda?
I haven't seen her.
Seriously? Don't tell Paimon she's ditched us on our first mission together...
I don't believe so. Nefer and I have our differences, but that shouldn't interfere with our shared objective.
Recovering the relic is my duty — but as far as she's concerned, there's plenty to gain here too.
In Nod-Krai, it's common knowledge that the Curatorium has a nose for profit and opportunity... the same way aphids flit from flower to flower in a neverending quest to make honey.
Huh. Sounds like you know her pretty well...

dialogue.sit: (Maybe a bit TOO well...)
(...And that's exactly why there's a rift between them.)

dialogue.t: Still, Jahoda sure is taking her sweet time...
...I believe we may have misjudged and underestimated Miss Jahoda.
Huh? What do you mean?
As a... former employee of the Curatorium, I'm confident that she possesses both professionalism and integrity in ample measure.
Eh? What was that noise?
The sound of a wavering conscience, perhaps?
Aah!
Whoa, something just fell down!
Ahaha... Hi—Hello everybody!
What kind of an entrance is that!? Wait a second... Have you been hiding nearby this whole time?
Uh... Y—Yeah! I was just, uh... scouting things out from up high!
(Darn it...! How did Jane Doe even notice me up there?)
(*sigh*... Can't believe I only realized I'd run out of smoke bombs this morning... What if something goes wrong inside? How am I supposed to make a quick getaway now...?)
(Thought I could just hang back and wait for the clients to get cold feet, but nope... Turns out they're all completely fearless! Don't they know how scary the Fatui are!?)
Um... Really sorry, everyone... Truth is, just as I was heading out this morning, I discovered I'd run out of a super important, completely essential, absolutely indispensable piece of equipment...
Uh... So, what are we gonna do?
Hehe... Well, as I see it, there are two options!
Plan A is... We take a detour to Nasha Town to restock. Though who knows if any shops will still be open this late...
Plan B is... We call it quits right here, disband the team, and all go home! My place is only, like, a ten-minute walk from here, so...
Personally, I vote Plan B! Bada bing, bada boom! Maximum efficiency, minimal effort!
Don't try to solve your problems by running away!

dialogue.sit: Neither of those "plans" sound great...

dialogue.t: Not a fan of either? Then I guess our only option is to fall back on Plan J — that's J for Jahoda, by the way!
Uh... Why didn't you just tell us that was an option in the first place?
C'mon, that would've totally ruined the surprise! Boss pulls this trick all the time, and it's always the clueless ones who end up praising her to the skies...
Feels like you just threw shade at a whole lot of people...
I have faith in your professionalism, Jahoda. You don't need those flashy tricks — your abilities alone are more than enough to earn our respect.
(Huh, this Jane Doe sure has an eye for talent... Speaking of which, maybe it's time I started calling her something nicer?)
Hehe... You really mean that, Ja— I mean, Lauma Doe?
I do.
Tell you what, it's not every day you get to work alongside such considerate clients! I have a feeling we're gonna make a great team!
Plan J is this: we find our way in through the freight access on the facility's east side!
It's tucked away from view, and security's lighter at night. I've prepared some special gadgets too, so we should be ready for anything.
If we want this to go without a hitch, we'll need to work together every step of the way — so everyone, stick close behind me.
Now that finally sounds like a real pro talking...
Hey! You saying I didn't before!?
Uh... Kinda, yeah...
You...! Ugh... Never mind. A top-tier treasure hunter like me never lets the naysayers get to her...
Alright, let's go over what we agreed on yesterday...
The goal of infiltrating the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau is to locate and, if possible, recover the relic that the Fatui stole.
We also need to figure out why they built the facility in the first place. I'm worried that they've set their sights on the Ancient Moon's Remnants on Hiisi Island, too.
Well, now that we've got a plan, time to get this show on the road..
Everyone, ready? Yeah? Then, let's move.

dialogue.sit: Let's go.
I need a little more time.

dialogue.t: Alright then, let's get this job done!
Just as I thought, there's a gate controlling access from the outside. Good thing I brought this key card, huh...
(Well, technically I stole it... but no need to tell them that, right? Blame that chump who thought it was a good idea to get wasted at The Flagship during work hours...)
Ooh! Is it top-level clearance?
Course, that goes without saying! Let me read it out for you...
Fatui Experimental Design Bureau No. 183574, maximum clearance... "Maintenance Intern."
...That doesn't sound very top-level to Paimon!
Never underestimate interns! Even the most legendary of thieves started out as rookie pickpockets, y'know?
Besides, if it wasn't for this person's selfless generosity, we wouldn't be able to just waltz in like this, would we?
Feels like you're trying really hard to change the subject...
Ahem... Allow me to teach you the first rule of treasure hunting...
"First and foremost — use every resource at your disposal!"
...Ahh, I get it now. It's like a pair of lightbulbs just lit up in my head...
Uhh... What did you just "get"?
The blue light, aka Plan A, is telling me to take the path along the left side. It'll be a lot stealthier, but that might mean a bit of a detour.
The red light, aka Plan B, is saying: "Just charge straight in!" But that'll mean dealing with... like, a dozen sentry bots already powering up.
Although... I might be able to switch them to "training mode." Their attacks will be weaker, but we'll still be in for a fight.
Can't you just put them in "sleep mode"...?
Hey, I told you I'm just a Maintenance Intern! Give the new recruit some time and space to blossom, will ya?
(Hmm... We're still pretty close to the entrance. Surely they'll call the whole thing off once they see what these bots can do?)
Anyway, I say we go with Plan B. Either way, I won't be doing any of the fighting, so... the shorter route sounds good to me!
If we can avoid fighting at this stage, we should.

dialogue.sit: No Plan J this time?

dialogue.t: Plan J... is to call it a night so we can all make it back to bed before sunrise! After all, the deeper we go, the more dangerous this is gonna get — so we might as well give up while we still can!

dialogue.sit: Let's take the stealthy route.
Let's charge straight in.

dialogue.t: Okay, you're the bosses...
Just don't forget — whatever you do, don't let those recon bots spot you!
Let's see... Huh, no kidding! Ineffa told me about something like this before. Can't believe that dumb robot actually helped me out for once...
All you gotta do is... this, and the recon bots will be reassigned to another position.
That way, when it's time to move forward, the path will be clear! Which reminds me, it's about time I taught you the third rule of treasure hunting...
"Go with the flow!"
What about the second one? You skipped that one...
Huh, did I? Oh jeez, I must've gotten them muddled up again...
...I—I mean... the second rule is exactly the same as the first!
Guess that's what you meant by going with the flow, huh...
Hey! There's someone up ahead.
Has the lockdown been initiated? Move it, soldier — the cargo has already been transferred.
The lockdown procedure is complete, commander. That sector is now fully sealed.
Tch, the night shift... Just our luck. Don't they usually handle deliveries during the daytime? There's not supposed to be anyone here...
(We've come this far already, and they're really trying their best... If I suggest backing out again, it's not gonna look good. Come on, brain, think!)
...Ah, I've got it! The freight shaft to the upper levels... We might have a shot there.
Let me see... Huh? The recon bot in the middle's not responding? ...A double-lock failsafe!? Ugh, we've been outfoxed!
Stay calm, stay calm... One step at a time. Let's just find a way across first...
What do we do now? There are guards here too...
Don't worry, bots are way easier to deal with than people. At least their behavior is predictable.
First, let's find a safe spot to land... Good, that spot shouldn't draw their attention. Let's go.
Let me just try something... Mmm... Maybe I can use the terminal to command them to move out of our way...
Security verification? With ten questions!? Are you kidding me!?!

dialogue.sit: You've got this, Jahoda!
Don't waste your energy. Let's just fight them.

dialogue.t: You really trust me that much? Ugh, fine... I'll... do my best.
But just to be clear — if I can't answer a question, I'm backing straight out of the terminal. No way I'm risking triggering any sort of alarm...

dialogue.sit: That's fine. You've got this.

dialogue.t: (Come on, Jahoda... You can't give up now!)
Question One... "What is our motto?"... Oh, I—I know this one...
Question Five... The name of the Harbinger in charge of this facility... Let's go with... "Sandrone."
This one should be... The "Palestar Edict." I've heard one of Boss's informants mention that before...
Final question... Enter employee ID? And it's timed!? Okay, okay... 183574... Confirm!
I... actually got them all right!? What a miracle...
Not bad, Jahoda, not bad at all! Guess you're an official Maintenance Intern now, hehe...
Hey, that could be my personal "Plan B" if I can't get my job back... Hehe, just kidding... The Fatui are awful.
The bots have taken the command... they're moving off. Let's get going while the coast is clear.
Here, bucket bucket bucket... Where are you hiding?
Judging from the concentration of kuuvahki... over there.
Wow! You can sense that, Lauma Doe? That's incredible...
Let's move the recon bots above them out of the way first.
Didn't think they'd even cut off the supply of kuuvahki... They're being really cautious.
If we can somehow divert some emergency power into the system, we might be able to force boot this thing.
What do you mean by "force boot"?
Uh, how do I explain this... It's like... dumping a whole bucket of water into an empty pool? So that... the little ducky gets to swim around again?
You should probably just ask Aino instead...
So we just need to find that bucket of water, right? Paimon thought your explanation was great! Kinda adorable, in a childish sort of way.
Hey, you could've just skipped that last part!
Is this what you were looking for?
That's right, that's exactly what we needed. Where did you find that?
I sensed kuuvahki inside it during the fight just now. They must've been using it as backup energy for their armor.
I honestly had no idea that fighting could solve so many problems... Darn it, why am I so weak?
Oops, did I say that out loud? Ahaha, just, uh... ignore me...
Oh, it's so dark in here...
Well, it is a cargo crate, after all. No point being picky about lighting at this point...
Whaaa! Something sharp and pointy just poked me in the back...!
Ah... Sorry, that was probably just my antlers. It's pretty cramped in here, so I had to crouch down...
Having antlers must be inconvenient at times like these...
Zzzzt!
Aaah... What's going on!?
(Don't tell me something's gone wrong already!?)
Ahem... Looks like there was only enough juice in the emergency power supply to lift us this far up...
(Ugh, awkward... Am I gonna get docked for this? Based on the boss's policy of docking pay for every screw-up, I'm— No, wait a sec... I've already been fired...)
Doesn't look like it's moving again any time soon.
I—I think... we can get through if we follow the ventilation duct along the outer wall... The entrance has gotta be somewhere. Don't worry, this was... totally part of the plan!
Huh!?
Clang!
Jahoda!? How'd you end up outside?
Looks like she slipped out at the very last second, just before the gate shut. Impressive reflexes, I must say — though I'd expect nothing less from a former employee of the Curatorium.
I'm so sorry! That was pure survival instinct... I didn't mean to ditch you!
Anyway, you guys just stay where you are. I'll... I'll figure something out...
Hey, there's a terminal nearby. Hang tight!
...Can you hear me now?

dialogue.sit: Loud and clear.

dialogue.t: The duct's security protocol has been triggered... The gate must've dropped when it detected a living presence.
Wait, so... we're trapped in here!?
I'm checking what I can do from this end... Ah, watch out for the laser up ahead!
What laser...?
We see it now... Good thing we didn't move.

dialogue.sit: I don't think we can jump up right now...
We're being held down by the kuuvahki.

dialogue.t: Got it... I think I understand the situation! Hang in there, just one moment...
...Ugh, this is killing me, but I think I've got it. I can try adjusting the direction of the kuuvahki flow inside the duct.
If I've got this right, you might just be able to dodge the lasers by utilizing the kuuvahki's pull in reverse!
Ooh, Paimon thinks she gets what you mean.
But I can't see where you are from here, so I'll need your constant input. Just tell me what to do — I'll follow your lead.
We made it to the other side, and all thanks to Jahoda!
But... But the gate hasn't opened... How's she gonna meet up with us?
Jaho-daaaa...
"No irregularities detected in the duct." "Confirm." "Confirm." "Confirm."
Ugh! Just confirm the command already, you... useless excuse for a terminal, you piece of robo-junk, you... mindless pile of scrap!
What the... Insufficient clearance!? Of course I don't have the clearance, you oversized—
Urgh!!! ...Ouch...

(Go with the flow, Jahoda, go with the flow. If the others make progress, that's great — but you can't bank on it. You've never been one to depend on others... so it's about time you stepped up to the challenge.)
(Deep breaths... Stay calm.)
(My priority right now is getting my hands on a high-level access card. That way, I can override the security protocol.)
(Senior maintenance staff... Only they can access the core sector. But hey, there's always someone careless enough to hide a spare key under the flowerpot by the door...)
(Which means... there's a good chance there's a duplicate lying around somewhere in the control room!)

(Even if I can't get into the control room myself, doesn't mean I can't rely on some external help! If I can take control of one of those guard bots, maybe I can use it to search for the access card!)
This is crazy, Jahoda... You're all alone, you've got nothing, and yet you're charging ahead like fear's a foreign concept...
Haha, maybe that's exactly why — 'cause I've got nothing left to lose!
"Confirm!"
Am I... a genius?
Whoa, this feed's super clear... This is gonna be a piece of cake!
Wait a second... This thing's not a guard bot, it's a...
...Janitor bot!?
Let me see...
There it is...!
Hey, why'd you stop? You haven't finished sweeping that corner!
(But... I can see the card from here...!)
(Ugh... Guess I have no choice but to swallow my pride and stay in character for now...)

dialogue.sit: (test)台词文本

dialogue.t: But will Jahoda be okay?
(Paimon!?)
She said she'd use every resource at her disposal, so let's have some faith in her abilities. Besides, when it comes to surviving in Nod-Krai, she probably knows more than any of us...
(So they really do believe in me...)
But how long are we gonna have to stay here? Paimon doesn't wanna get caught by the Fatui either...
Does Paimon mean the two Fatui in that room? Let me see if there's a way to distract them...
...Wait, did you hear that?

dialogue.sit: Don't move.

dialogue.t: Huh? The alarm? What's going on?
Let's go check it out!

dialogue.sit: Now's our chance!

dialogue.t: This looks like somewhere important, but there's nothing here...
Hey guys, it's me!
Jahoda! Are you okay?
I'm fine!
I managed to swipe a high-level access card and triggered an alarm to draw the guards off... But we don't have much time.
Alright... Looks like we can control the elevator!
Come on, hop in. Let's take it further down.
There's no one here!
That's good news for us! Let's head inside.
Looks like a rest area for the Fatui's Oprichniki.
Huh? The terminal's still on...?
Ahaha... Looks like that "good news"... is now half good news, half bad news...
What do you mean?
Well, seems like that alarm I just triggered was so high-level that even the guards in the rest area went to investigate... that's the good news, by the way.
Then what's the bad news?
The bad news... is that once they realize it was a false alarm, they're bound to circle back and check this floor, and then we're toast!
So we've gotta move fast here! If you need me to run a quick search, say the word.

dialogue.sit: Information about the Moon Marrow...
A map of the facility...
The facility's purpose...

dialogue.t: "...Analysis of the kuuvahki extracted from the Moon Marrow suggests that its energy core bears some close relation to the power of the former Three Moon Sisters..."
"...It is suspected that there is a link between the Frostmoon Scions' hidden relic and the shattered remnants of the Eternal Moon..."
C'mon, none of this is important right now... Just tell us where you hid the darn thing!
"Access denied. You do not have permission to view this data."
Even with a high-level access card? Who does have permission then!?

dialogue.sit: Can't think of anything else...
A map of the facility...
The facility's purpose...

dialogue.t: Looks like that's about all our current clearance gives us access to...
Based on what we know so far, it seems like the rest must be hidden inside that massive hollow beneath us...
I could sense something beneath the water down there... something unsettling.
If they've gotten their hands on the Moon Marrow, odds are it's hidden down there too.
(Ugh... and here I thought we were almost done. But nope, we're going deeper and deeper into the danger zone...)
(Chin up, Jahoda! Once this job's done, you're buying yourself the biggest Nod-Kraian hot dog in town. Deal's a deal!)
That switch looks... suspiciously obvious. No way I'm pulling that! But you guys, go ahead...
Hey, you spotted it first! Shouldn't you be the one to pull it?
Not a chance! I'm just the guide, remember? At most, I'll help you look for an escape route...
(They don't seriously think pulling this thing's gonna lead to treasure, do they? I'd be amazed if it doesn't set off an alarm...)
(Besides, I didn't even bring my smoke bombs... Which reminds me of the actual second rule of treasure hunting: "Better safe than sorry!")

dialogue.sit: Allow me.

dialogue.t: *Rumbling*
The ground... it's shaking!
Wait, did the...
...Surface of the water... open up?
This is bad... this is really bad... I'm getting put on the Fatui's blacklist for sure...
Don't worry, Jahoda, you've helped us so much. If they try anything, we'll protect you!
C'mon, I—I was just kidding! I'm tough, okay... Just haven't had a chance to show off my fighting skills yet. Me, afraid of the Fatui? Not a chance!
I suspect the relic is hidden down below. Jahoda, your commission ends here.
I am truly grateful for everything you've done for us. You don't need to put yourself in any further danger.
I'm coming with you.
This has nothing to do with the commission, or the danger, or whatever... This has already gotten way out of hand, so I'm coming too — end of story!
She's blushing...
Hey, zip it! Why d'you keep staring... You looking for a knuckle sandwich, or what? C'mon, move it already!
It's really deep down here... What is this place?
...We're standing on another fragment of the Ancient Moon's Remnants.
(So this was the source of the kuuvahki I sensed earlier...)
Wait, what!? So the Fatui had it hidden underwater this whole time? This gigantic thing!?
Jahoda, you've... been kinda quiet since we got down here...
Wha— Me? Have I? Haha... It's nothing, really...
(Ugh, we're doomed... How are we even supposed to get back up from here?)
(My grappling hook's not nearly long enough... and if someone spots us here after all that commotion... we'll be sitting ducks!)
Eek!
Ah! Oh no, that door's opening! Please don't say it's the Fatui...!
(No, please, no! We finally made it here, and we're so close to getting the job done... I didn't risk my neck just to die before I've even had a chance to spend my reward!)
...What happened? Why did the underwater barrier open?
How could this be...?
Huh...? Lauma? And... you guys?
Vilemina... What's going on here?
Looks like... there's no point trying to hide it anymore...
Wh—What are you talking about?
I thought you might come, but I didn't expect to see you here so soon... Forget it, the Moon Marrow isn't here.
You... joined the Fatui?
...Yes.
...When?
...The day I could no longer bear to live a lie!
At first, the Fatui wouldn't accept me... But then one of their Harbingers noticed me, and... said she'd give me a chance...
Ugh... Lost them again...
(That Harbinger... told me to follow the blond(blonde) Traveler who might visit the Frostmoon Scions...)
(*sigh*... Easier said than done, though. The animals are on alert at night... If they see me, Lauma will catch wind of what I'm doing, sooner or later...)
(...Am I really doing the right thing?)
(No... It's too late to turn back now. The empty prayers, the stubborn displays of faith, like Kapy's today... This isn't the life I want.)
(Huh? Is that... Ah! {NICKNAME}'s back! I won't let him(her) slip away this time!)
(Wait. Who's that with him(her)? They look so alike... Hmm, they seem to be heading... towards the statue of Kuutar!)
(They've... opened the secret chamber!? But... wasn't it meant to be sealed?)
Wait a second... the Moon Marrow!
(Surely they're not after the Moon Marrow!? I'd better go report this straight to...)
Hold on...
(If they do actually make it to the final room... then maybe I'll be able to get my hands on the relic... the one thing the Fatui have been after this whole time...)
(If someone's going to take it, it might as well be me... This could be my ticket to joining them!)

dialogue.sit: That night... it was you.
You followed us in...

dialogue.t: Yes... and in your final moment of hesitation, I... took the chance...
...And then you gave it to the Fatui!?
But... when we talked to you before, you seemed so genuinely worried about Lauma...
Because I... I thought she was as fed up with the Frostmoon Scions as I was!
We grew up together, Lauma. I know you were chosen to be the next Moonchanter when you were just a child. They never gave you a choice in that.
I saw the look in your eyes when you were treating that child... that sense of helplessness. Surely you, too, must see that this blind, inherited faith of ours is simply holding us back...
If our prayers are never answered... then why keep praying? Do they really deserve all of your devotion?
Or... are you trapped by the responsibilities they imposed on you?
So those are your reasons for wanting to leave the Frostmoon Scions?
Isn't that reason enough!?
*sigh*... When we pray to the moon, we do so to show our gratitude for the life it granted us long ago. It reminds us to strive for something higher within ourselves...
But I know that's not what you want to hear. You're right, Vilemina... I have indeed kept secrets from you.

dialogue.sit: (Lauma...)

dialogue.t: I knew it... You don't want to be the Moonchanter, do you...?
No, that's not it. I'm talking about the fact that the moon in the sky isn't real.
What...? Y—You're saying... Huh?
(Ugh, I've completely lost the thread now... but do we really have to do this here? What if a Harbinger shows up... I'm not cut out for fighting big bosses!)
The pain you sensed in me... was the pain of hiding this truth.
If what you're saying is true, then you already knew that the Frostmoon Scions wouldn't believe any of this... Why didn't you just leave, like I did?
You don't understand, do you? That's the difference between us, Vilemina — I care about the Frostmoon Scions. They're family to me.
It hurts because I care... and that's why I chose to hide the truth. But now I understand — that was a mistake.
My family deserves to know the truth. I shouldn't have tried to hold it all together with empty prayers...
Hah... Are you trying to say that I only ever cared about myself?
There's nothing wrong with that, in itself. No one would have tried to stop you from leaving... but you did not have to stab us in the back like this.
...We've been spotted!
(I knew it, I just knew it! Ugh, what now!? If a Harbinger shows up, I'm outta here. No darned relic is worth dying over!)
...Looks like I misjudged you, Lauma. I didn't think you had it in you to stand up to your fate.
Turns out... you are a great Moonchanter, after all.
But you were right about one thing — I haven't considered Hiisi Island my home for a long, long time now.
Bosses, time to go!
I will change the Frostmoon Scions, Vilemina... as soon as the new moon rises.
...Then I guess I won't be around to see it.
Say, Lauma — what happens to those who betray the Frostmoon Scions?
"...May their antlers be shorn with silver blades... and let them be cast into the long night of unknowing."
Ugh... Ahhh... Aaaaagh!!!
...I have honored the ways of the Frostmoon Scions, one last time... Think of it as a gesture of respect, Lauma.
There they are!
Lauma!
Marionette has the Moon Marrow... She went to Starsand Shoal.
Don't... flatter yourself, now — I'm not trying to "atone." I just... don't believe you'll actually be able to change them...
(Hmm...? An alarm? Coming from the Experimental Design Bureau?)
Hm... Interesting.
Hey, wrap things up and get yourselves ready... Looks like we might be having some guests.
Yes, my Lady...
Perfect timing... this job's been boring me to death. Time to test some hypotheses.
Bosses... I mean, esteemed clients... I mean, generous benefactors... Wait up, c'mon!
Sure you don't wanna consider heading home first and coming back another day...? Nasha Town's that way! You are aware that this is the way to... Ahhhh!
A little ahead of schedule, aren't you?
(Oh no, it really is a Harbinger this time...!)
Marionette...
So you are here, after all! Hand over that relic, right now — it belongs to the Frostmoon Scions!
Mm? You mean that thing your antlered turncoat brought us?
Ha... I have never much cared for trophies given up without a fight. But watching you tear each other apart over it? Priceless.
...I'm not in the mood for warnings today.
Ooh, how frightening. Had I a "tremble" function, I'd have rattled off at least a dozen screws by now.
Or perhaps I've just set my "sense of humor" parameter too high. Were you trying to be funny just now?
You don't honestly believe you're a match for me... Do you?
Go on, then. Let's serve our guests a little appetizer...
Hey, didn't you hear me? I said let's serve our guests a little—
Wh—What's going on?
...Oh no! Watch out, {NICKNAME}!
It's the Wild Hunt!
Is that... it?
Whew... At least, that's what the Lightkeepers' handbook says...
Careful! It's not over yet!

dialogue.sit: (What's going on...? It's Abyssal power alright, and even stronger than before...)
(What's the Wild Hunt even after...)
Paimon! Lauma! Jahoda!
(No response... I have to find them again, and quickly...)
Aether(Lumine)! Over here!
...! Lumine(Aether)!
Quick, grab my hand!
Aether(Lumine)...! What's wrong?
...Why are you here at all, Lumine(Aether)?
...What do you mean?

dialogue.t: If I may be so bold... What does "family" mean to you, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: ...Why were you after the Moon Marrow that night, Lumine(Aether)?

dialogue.t: Among those who entered the final chamber, there was either someone with impure intent, or else... an Abyssal presence.

dialogue.sit: We can talk about that later!
Tell me why, Lumine(Aether).
(No... It can't be...)
You know, this is only the second time we've fought together since the day we both woke up in Teyvat.
No...
...Aether(Lumine)?
But when I found you, you were still in hibernation. Even the key to the chamber was still secure on your person.
We... didn't wake up together...
What are you talking about? We don't have time for this, Aether(Lumine)!
Look at me, Aether(Lumine).
Don't you want to explore this world with me?

dialogue.t: Hey! Is everyone okay?
Whew... Think I saw my life flash before my eyes there. Good thing Lauma Doe was there to save the day...
Are you alright, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: I'm fine...

dialogue.t: Ha... Well, that took you long enough. Seriously, how many of you are there? Pathetic...
(Oh no... I spoke too soon! Totally forgot we still have a Harbinger to deal with!)
Hey, is that... the Moon Marrow! It was hidden inside that big robot of hers all along!
But... that robot...
Ugh... That's "Pulonia" to you, not just some "robot"!
...Take it, and get lost.
Huh? You're just... giving it to us?
Well, I wasn't the one who put out the order to find this thing in the first place... So if someone wants it, they can help themselves. Maybe even choke on it — see if I care.

dialogue.sit: (Is she saying... that it was another Harbinger who was after the Moon Marrow?)

dialogue.t: ...So? Are you waiting for me to change my mind, or what? I'd be more than happy to pick up where we just left off... But, I should warn you, I'm in a bad mood right now.
...Let's go.
Fine by me! Totally, completely, absolutely on board with that!
It's... finally over. *sigh* If that doesn't make the "Most Thrilling Commission of the Year," I don't know what will...
Looks like... the Fatui are all gone now... Agh!
Lauma!

dialogue.sit: (Lauma mentioned that she normally has to keep her power in check. I guess... this is what happens if she doesn't...)

dialogue.t: I'm alright... It's just been so long since I truly felt the power of the moon...
Hmm? I thought I sensed the Wild Hunt nearby... Don't tell me... you've already taken care of it?
Hey, it's Flins!
(Hey, he's... that Ratnik!)
Unless I am mistaken... You are the Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, are you not? May I ask... What is that in your hand?
Please, don't get me wrong. I've been tracking the Wild Hunt lately, and I've come to suspect that its actions... aren't as aimless as they might seem.
When I saw what you were holding, I could not help but start... connecting the dots.

dialogue.sit: (So that night, Lumine(Aether)... No, the Wild Hunt... was using me to get to the Moon Marrow...?)
(I'd better find some time to have a word with Flins, just in case...)

dialogue.t: You'd better be extra careful, Flins... It seems like the Wild Hunt is capable of impersonating people now.
Oh, is that so? Funny that — I just showed up completely out of the blue, yet you seem to have no problems trusting me...
Hahaha... I apologize. I shouldn't be making jokes like that right now.
Anyway, I understand — thank you for the tip-off. It seems that the Wild Hunt has somehow... changed in nature. I'll have to report this to HQ right away.
For now, let us part ways here.

dialogue.sit: (There's... still something strange about him that I can't seem to put my finger on...)

dialogue.t: Phew...

dialogue.sit: (Wait, so... Lauma was on her guard against him this whole time?)

dialogue.t: That little "joke" of his just now... sure scared the bejeebies out of Paimon. Are all the Ratniki in Nod-Krai like that...?
They're usually stationed in remote areas and tend to keep to themselves. So, uh, it's not surprising they end up a little... eccentric?
No... He's different.
Really? How so?
The animals... they've told me they're afraid to even go near him...
Oh, you're back. I just made you all a pot of tea — better drink it while it's hot.
Boss Nef, you wouldn't believe how scary our day has been! Seriously, I am never, ever taking random jobs like that, EVER again... Ya hear me?
Oh, come on, now! You even faced the Wild Hunt and lived to tell the tale... What's left to be afraid of?
Wait a sec, how did you— Ohhh right, like you told us before... Your business is "dealing in information."
Huh? Boss Nef... The teacups... Wh—Why is there one missing? Did you... think I wasn't coming back!?
My, my... How could you think that of me? You know the rules — if a member of staff wants tea, they pour it themselves. Your cup's sitting safe and sound, right there in the cupboard.
A... m—member of staff? Does that mean you're... accepting me back!?!
Wasn't that the deal?
Boss Nef! You're the best boss ever!
Heh. You never change, do you? Everything turned out fine, no? You found exactly what you were looking for... yet there you are, sulking away as usual.
Nefer... That medicine we discussed before, the one for congenital kuuvahki sensitivity... I need you to get it for me.
And how do you expect me to find something like that for you in the middle of the night? You'll have to wait till morning, at the very least.
I need it right now.
Alright, alright, I'll see what I can do. But you know "urgent" means "extra charge," right?
So... Thank you.
...Hmm. You know what? You do seem a little... different.
In a good way, or a bad way?
Mm... Who can say? I'll take it either way, so long as you don't start making a habit of asking me for ridiculous favors...
{NICKNAME}, Paimon... A lot has happened these past few days. I don't know what I would have done without you.
Hey, don't mention it! That's what we're here for!

dialogue.sit: Don't forget, your family believe and trust in you too.

dialogue.t: Mhm, you're right... and tonight, I'm planning on telling them everything.
Tonight? Isn't it a bit... late already?
The moon shines brightly this night... What better time for the Frostmoon Scions to usher in a new dawn for truth?

dialogue.sit: I'll support you...
...And be there for you.

dialogue.t: Thank you for your kind words.
But before I do, there's one more thing we need to deal with...
Ohhh, yeah... Now that we have the Moon Marrow...
You'll... have to forgive me... I used too much of my strength in the battle earlier. I fear... I won't be able to help you uncover the truth of the past. Not right away, at least.
That's fine! We're going to be in Nod-Krai for a while anyway, so there's no rush, right?

dialogue.sit: Your health is more important.
Besides, I trust you.

dialogue.t: Thank you.
But there's another problem... How to keep the Moon Marrow safe now.
Huh? Can't we just return it to your secret chamber?
The seal has been broken. Even if it were restored... now that the Wild Hunt has gotten in once, there's no guarantee that it won't happen again...
Oh, right... Yeah, that makes sense...
Back when the Frostmoon Scions' bloodline still ran strong, in special circumstances, a Moonchanter could act as a vessel, safeguarding the relic within their own body...
But it is a grueling trial of will and endurance. The Moonchanter who did this... only lasted two days.
As for me... I might be able to last five, at most.
Hold on... You'd be using your body as a vessel?
Yes. You can think of it like dropping a red-hot ball of iron into a bucket of water. How long the water lasts... depends entirely on the bucket's size.

dialogue.sit: If that's the case...
...Maybe I can give it a try?

dialogue.t: ...Pardon?
Hey, that's not a bad idea! You've always held up pretty well against the Abyss... Surely the Moon Marrow can't be any more dangerous than that?
I... It's not at all that I don't trust you, but... it's too risky.
But we're out of options, aren't we? Might as well give it a shot.

dialogue.sit: Paimon's right.
I'm willing to take the risk.

dialogue.t: ...Alright. Well, I'll be right by your side. If anything feels off, please tell me immediately.

dialogue.sit: What do I need to do?

dialogue.t: Here, hold it in your hands.
Feel its power... Imagine you're a lake, a cluster of stars... Let the moon become a part of you...
Wh—Whoa! It... went into your body!
How was that? Are you feeling any discomfort?

dialogue.sit: ...None at all.
(But... I seem more attuned to the kuuvahki than I was before...)
(When I close my eyes... I can sense something far off, beyond the false sky... So that's the true Frost Moon?)

dialogue.t: Astonishing... Not even the slightest hint of lingering fluctuations. It's as if all that power... just sank to the bottom of the ocean.
Well, looks like we won't have to worry about the Wild Hunt catching its scent now...
Whew, Paimon knew you have special abilities, but still, you never fail to amaze.
...Mm? Did I miss something just now?
Yes... and it was nothing short of a miracle...
Ha, not something I'd be interested in, then. Anyway, here's the medicine you asked for. This is all I've got for today — I'll have someone send the rest over when we have it.
Thank you, Nefer. I really appreciate everything you've done for me.
Please stop being so... nauseatingly friendly. It's creeping me out.
So... What exactly did you all go through during that Wild Hunt attack? I'd prefer to hear it straight from you.
Hmm... A phantom that can mimic the appearance of others... Quite different from what we've seen before.

dialogue.sit: It disappeared right in front of me...
...But I think it'll be back.

dialogue.t: Yeah... and both times it appeared, its goal was pretty clear. It seems like it was after the Moon Marrow!
...And on both occasions, it was accompanied by the Wild Hunt too. It appears there must be some close connection between the two.
I must say, I don't often see you look this serious, Nefer.
Too late in the day for thinking, that's all. We'll pick this up again later. You all feel free to keep chatting, though — just don't forget to lock up when you leave.
On that note... {NICKNAME}, please keep the Moon Marrow stored within your body for the time being.
We'll take it back off your hands as soon as the Wild Hunt's been taken care of, once and for all...

dialogue.sit: Sure thing. Trust me, I've got this.
Aren't you worried I'll make a run for it?

dialogue.t: Of course.
Anyway, if the two of you will excuse me... I'm heading back to Hiisi Island now. It's time I came clean with the Frostmoon Scions.
Hey, we're coming with you! Though... guess we won't be able to do much more than cheer you on from the sidelines.
That alone means more to me than you could ever know.
...What's going on?
I'm not sure. Seems like the Moonchanter has something important to tell us...
I heard the relic's already been retrieved.
That's our Lady Lauma, alright!
*deep breath*

dialogue.sit: (Do what you believe is right, Lauma...)

dialogue.t: Noble scions of the Frost Moon... My kin beneath the moonlight...
I hereby declare the truth to you...
"Long have our ancestors looked up to the Frost Moon, guided by her serene light... Yet now, she lies hidden beyond the limits of the sky."

dialogue.sit: And so, Lauma began to reveal to the Frostmoon Scions a truth long hidden within her heart... A story of a false moon, and the death of gods...

dialogue.t: "Kuutar was indeed born of the moon... but that does not give us the right to reap without sowing, nor clothe ourselves without the toil of weaving..."

dialogue.sit: As she spoke, some who listened were stunned into disbelief, while others... seemed to awaken, as if from a dream.

dialogue.t: "...From this day forth, the road shall be paved with truth, and we shall pave it ourselves."
Whew... After everything Lauma said last night, Paimon wonders how everyone's adjusting...

dialogue.sit: Well, we're here to find out...

dialogue.t: Still, judging by their reactions at the time, it didn't seem as intense as Paimon might have imagined... Says a lot about how much trust she commands, huh?
Hey, look — it's Lauma!
Welcome, both of you. The animals were most lively this morning... They told me of your coming.

dialogue.sit: Has everything been okay?

dialogue.t: Nothing too dramatic happened, did it? No one took it so hard that they went on a binge eating rampage, and ended up cleaning up the whole pantry... or something?

dialogue.sit: The only person who would do something like that is you, Paimon.

dialogue.t: Hey, Paimon's just trying to lighten the mood...
Thank you for your concern.
Change doesn't happen overnight, and new ideas need time to take root... But nothing as extreme as that has happened, no.
Although...
A—Although what?
Well... Just as I thought might happen, some have chosen to leave the Frostmoon Scions for good. For them, losing their faith was like losing their home.
Confusion, frustration, helplessness... I saw it all, reflected in their eyes.
Oh...
I respect their choice. May they carry the Frostmoon Scions' blessings far and wide — should they be willing to do so.
If we meet again someday, perhaps we will be able to sit together and share stories once more.

dialogue.sit: Hope everything goes well for them...

dialogue.t: Others sought me out afterward, though... and thanked me profusely for sharing the truth with our people.
They said they used to see me as "distant," even somewhat unapproachable... Whereas now, I seemed much closer to them — like a friend, or even a family member.
Sounds like a win overall! Paimon thinks you did the right thing, Lauma.
Thank you...
Though, I wanted to ask...
Do I really come across as... "distant"?
W—Well... maybe just a little, to people who don't know you? You are kinda tall... especially if you consider the antlers...
I see...
That's a bit of a hard one... My antlers tend to grow under the moonlight, so I can't quite help it.

dialogue.sit: Just be yourself. No need to act any different...
Family should be honest with each other, after all...

dialogue.t: It brings me comfort to hear you say that.
By the way, {NICKNAME}, how has your body been adjusting to the Moon Marrow?

dialogue.sit: I'm feeling absolutely fine.

dialogue.t: I'm glad to hear it. I've also suggested to Nefer that we meet within the next few days. We need to figure out how to counter this new manifestation of the Wild Hunt.
But for now... let's just relax.
I want to enjoy this feeling a little longer... of finally living on the bright side of the moon.

quests.description: Ever do ominous mists rise at night, and ever will perilous schemes brew in the darkness…
